title: The Meaning Behind Pakistan’s First Lunar Rover
author: Usman Haider
text:
An early prototype of the track system for Pakistan’s first lunar rover, dubbed the Jinnah 1.
Credit: SUPARCO
The lunar South Pole has emerged as a major focus of international space exploration due to its scientific potential. In view of this, Pakistan has also decided to send its own scientific mission there. The country’s first indigenous lunar rover, Jinnah 1, will head to the Moon’s South Pole in 2029 aboard China’s Chang’e 8 mission. Pakistan’s decision to undertake a lunar mission reflects three key perspectives. First, the gesture is symbolic as Islamabad also wants to be among the group of elite member countries conducting scientific research on the Moon, indicating its growing interest in the space sector. Second, the mission signals the revival of an old rivalry on the Moon, as India reached the lunar South Pole with Chandrayaan 3 in 2023. Lastly, Jinnah 1 illustrates increasing cooperation between Pakistan and China in the space domain. [...]
